key_insight: A SCAPS-1D + machine learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell stacks and uncover high-efficiency, lead-free architectures with clear physical drivers.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical design strategy for screening ETL/absorber/HTL combinations, reducing trial-and-error while guiding interface-aware optimization for scalable perovskite PV devices.
method: Simulated 125 device architectures across 5 ETLs, 5 absorbers, and 5 HTLs using SCAPS-1D.
Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for untested structures.
Used Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation and SHAP to validate ranking performance and identify key descriptors.
evidence_signal: The workflow identified and then confirmed high-performing devices, including FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.85% PCE and FTO/SnO2/Cs2AgInBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.62%, with eight of the top-11 designs using Cs2AgInBr6.
watch_item: The results depend on the fidelity of SCAPS assumptions and the training coverage of the sampled design space, so transfer to fabricated devices may require experimental validation.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
